title: Mali Empire
summary: The Mali Empire was a West African state that World History Encyclopedia dates from around 1240, when Sundiata Keita founded it with Niani as capital. It controlled gold-producing regions and the gold-for-salt trade, doubled in size under Mansa Musa, and lost power in the 1460s after civil wars and the rise of Songhai; a small western remnant lasted longer.

uncertainty.note: Start follows c. 1240 in two sources; the encyclopedia also prints 1235 and 1230 for the origin in other places. End is the c. 1468 Songhai conquest of the rump state; a small western pocket survived to the mid-17th century (World History Encyclopedia gives 1645 or c. 1672 as outer end dates).

importance.justification: One of the largest West African states, tied to the trans-Saharan gold trade and to Mansa Musa.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the end date (sources print 1460s, 1645 and c. 1672) and of the exact Niani site: the pages say only that it was probably on a plain near the Sankarani River, so the pin uses the GeoNames village of Niani with a wide radius.
